title: Add stepped trail parity faults and stop never moves down regression tests
description:
Create end-to-end-in-process lifecycle and fault regression tests for stepped trailing protection in tests/integration/test_stepped_trailing_lifecycle.py, and a verification audit document at docs/verification/phase_o_stepped_stops.md. This is a verification task: write real tests and a real audit artifact, and do not modify production code.

Before editing, inspect: mike_trade/risk/trailing.py (o.1), mike_trade/execution/replace.py and mike_trade/brokers/alpaca/replacement.py (o.2), mike_trade/execution/close_coordinator.py (o.3), mike_trade/risk/trailing_state.py (o.4), and their tests (tests/unit/test_stepped_trailing.py, tests/contracts/test_stop_replacement.py, tests/integration/test_stop_close_races.py, tests/unit/test_trailing_state_restart.py) to reuse fakes and fixtures without editing them.

Write integration tests that wire the ratchet (o.1), replacement coordinator with the in-memory fake port (o.2), close coordinator (o.3), and trailing state store on temporary SQLite (o.4) together, and cover:
1. Canonical lifecycle: entry 100, distance 2, step 1. After a confirmed positive fill, the initial broker-confirmed stop is 98. High 100.80 -> no replace request. High 101 -> intent persisted, then confirmed at 99. High 103.20 -> single replace to 101 (multi-step jump). A decline leaves 101 and produces no replace request.
2. Stop-never-moves-down regression: a randomized or parameterized price path (seeded and deterministic) asserts that the confirmed stop series is non-decreasing and that no broker replace call ever carries a price <= the prior confirmed stop after rounding.
3. Parity: for the same price path, the pure ratchet candidate sequence and the persisted/confirmed stop sequence agree whenever all replacements confirm.
4. Faults: replace rejected (last verified stop retained, TRAIL_UPDATE_UNCONFIRMED, entries blocked); replace unknown followed by lookup-based reconciliation; stop fill during replace; partial stop fill during replace (remaining quantity protected correctly); discretionary close racing a pending replace (no short, no duplicate sell); no duplicate pending replacements under rapid highs; orphan stop detection after flat.
5. Restart: persist mid-cycle with an outstanding intent, reload, and assert that advancement stays blocked until reconciliation, then resumes from the persisted watermark/anchor.
6. Engine offline: mark stale. The last confirmed stop remains and the status reports TRAIL_STALE. New highs while stale do not advance or submit replacements.
7. Protection begins only after a confirmed positive fill, and protected quantity equals actual remaining filled quantity.

Write docs/verification/phase_o_stepped_stops.md as an audit artifact with these contents: a table mapping each phase-o requirement (monotone ratchet, canonical example, rounding-before-compare, broker-confirmed effectiveness, intent-before-submit, no duplicate pending, unknown/rejected handling, fill-during-replace, close race/no-short, orphan detection, restart, offline TRAIL_STALE, fail-closed capability) to the specific test function names that prove it; the exact targeted pytest commands used; their observed pass/fail results; and an explicit statement of limitations. Those limitations must say that fakes are not broker integration evidence, that Alpaca paper verification is credential-gated and not performed here, and that no profitability claim is made.

If a test exposes a production defect, do not fix production code. Mark the test with an explicit xfail(strict=True) carrying a reason, and record the defect in the audit document.
acceptance_criteria: tests/integration/test_stepped_trailing_lifecycle.py exists and exercises the o.1 ratchet, the o.2 replacement coordinator (fake port), the o.3 close coordinator, and the o.4 state store together.

The canonical lifecycle test asserts that the confirmed stops are exactly Decimal 98, 99, 101, and that the stop remains 101 after a decline, with exactly two replace requests (to 99 and to 101) and none for high 100.80 or the decline.
A seeded deterministic regression test asserts a non-decreasing confirmed stop series and that no replace request price is <= the prior confirmed stop after rounding.

Fault tests cover rejected replace, unknown replace with reconciliation, full and partial stop fill during replace, discretionary close racing a pending replace (no negative position), duplicate-pending suppression, and orphan stop after flat.
A restart test proves that advancement is blocked with an outstanding intent after reload and resumes from the persisted watermark/anchor after reconciliation.
An offline/stale test proves that TRAIL_STALE is reported, the last confirmed stop is retained, and no replacement is submitted while stale.

docs/verification/phase_o_stepped_stops.md contains a requirement-to-test mapping table naming concrete test functions, the targeted commands run with observed results, and explicit limitations (fakes are not broker integration; Alpaca paper verification is credential-gated and pending; no profitability claim).
No production files under mike_trade/ are modified by this task.
tests/integration/test_stepped_trailing_lifecycle.py passes when run alone with pytest, or any failing case is marked xfail(strict=True) with a reason and documented as a defect in the audit file.
forbidden_changes: modify any production module under mike_trade/ or any test file written by o.1-o.4
change PLAN_SKELETON.json or other planning artifacts
claim broker integration or profitability based on fakes
access broker credentials, create live or paper orders, or run broad test suites/backtests
